title: Explain the Purpose of Organizational Processes and Procedures

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: A working network is not necessarily a manageable network. Documentation, life-cycle procedures, change controls, and known-good configurations let administrators understand what exists, where it is, how it connects, who supports it, when it should be replaced, what changed, and what correct operation looks like.
bullets: Physical, logical, rack, cable, and Layer 1-3 diagrams
Hardware, software, licensing, and warranty inventories
IPAM, SLAs, wireless surveys, and heat maps
EOL, EOS, software management, and decommissioning
sections.callout: DOCUMENT → TRACK → MAINTAIN → CHANGE → CONFIGURE → RETIRE

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: If someone new had to operate or troubleshoot the network tomorrow, identify the information and processes they would need to understand what exists, what changed, and what the environment should look like.
bullets: Real placement and connections → Physical diagram
Cable paths and endpoints → Cable map
Switching and VLAN relationships → Layer 2 diagram
IP and routing relationships → Layer 3 diagram

sections.title: Documentation
paragraphs: Documentation records important information about the network and supporting systems. Good documentation prevents the next administrator from guessing and improves troubleshooting, maintenance, upgrades, audits, and disaster recovery.
sections.callout: Document the environment so knowledge survives staff and technology changes.

entries.title: Physical Diagram
paragraphs: A physical diagram represents equipment, ports, cables, racks, physical links, and real locations—things an administrator can physically touch.
entries.recognitionCue: Actual cable or device placement → Physical diagram.

entries.title: Logical Diagram
paragraphs: A logical diagram emphasizes how the network functions: networks, VLANs, subnets, routing relationships, and logical connections rather than exact placement.
entries.recognitionCue: VLAN, subnet, or functional relationship → Logical diagram.

entries.title: Rack Diagram
paragraphs: A rack diagram shows where equipment is positioned in a rack, available rack space, and the organization of installed devices.
entries.recognitionCue: Locate a particular switch inside a rack → Rack diagram.

sections.title: Cable Maps and Layer 1-3 Network Diagrams

entries.title: Cable Maps and Diagrams
paragraphs: Cable maps trace cable origins and destinations, patch-panel ports, switch ports, wall connections, and device endpoints.

entries.title: Layer 1 Diagram
paragraphs: A Layer 1 diagram focuses on physical devices, cables, interfaces, and physical links.

entries.title: Layer 2 Diagram
paragraphs: A Layer 2 diagram focuses on switches, VLANs, data-link connections, and switching relationships.

entries.title: Layer 3 Diagram
paragraphs: A Layer 3 diagram focuses on IP networks, subnets, routers, Layer 3 interfaces, and routing relationships.

sections.callout: Physical links → Layer 1. Switching/VLANs → Layer 2. IP/routing → Layer 3.

sections.title: Asset Inventory
paragraphs: An asset inventory answers: What technology does the organization own, operate, or manage? Useful records include models, serial numbers, locations, ownership, deployment status, and support information.

entries.title: Hardware
paragraphs: Tracks physical assets such as routers, switches, access points, servers, and workstations.

entries.title: Software
paragraphs: Tracks deployed applications and versions for management, compatibility, security, and support.

entries.title: Licensing
paragraphs: Records authorized software use and the number of licenses available or consumed.

entries.title: Warranty Support
paragraphs: Records whether hardware remains eligible for manufacturer or vendor support and replacement.

entries.title: IP Address Management (IPAM)
paragraphs: IPAM centrally tracks address ranges, subnets, allocated addresses, and available addresses.

entries.title: Service-Level Agreement (SLA)
paragraphs: An SLA defines agreed and measurable service expectations such as availability, response time, or restoration targets.

entries.title: Wireless Survey and Heat Map
paragraphs: A wireless survey measures wireless conditions in a physical space. A heat map visualizes coverage or signal characteristics and helps reveal weak areas and gaps.
entries.memoryHook: Where is Wi-Fi strong or weak?

sections.title: Life-Cycle Management
paragraphs: Technology moves through deployment, maintenance, updates, and retirement. Life-cycle management plans these stages so unsupported or obsolete systems do not become operational and security risks.

entries.title: End-of-Life (EOL)
paragraphs: EOL means a product has reached the end of its product lifecycle and is being discontinued or retired.

entries.title: End-of-Support (EOS)
paragraphs: EOS means the vendor stops providing support for the product.

entries.title: Decommissioning
paragraphs: Decommissioning is the controlled removal of equipment or systems from production. It includes handling connections, configuration, data, ownership records, and dependent processes—not merely unplugging the device.

sections.callout: EOL is product retirement; EOS is support termination. They can occur at different times.

entries.title: Patches and Bug Fixes
paragraphs: Patches and bug fixes correct security vulnerabilities, stability issues, and functional defects.

entries.title: Operating System (OS)
paragraphs: Operating systems require tracked versions, updates, compatibility planning, and lifecycle management.

entries.title: Firmware
paragraphs: Firmware is software embedded in or closely associated with hardware. Routers, switches, and APs may require firmware updates for bugs, security, compatibility, or features.
entries.recognitionCue: A low-level vendor update for a network appliance → Firmware.

sections.title: Change Management
paragraphs: Change management provides a controlled, documented process for modifying production technology. It records what will change, why it is needed, who requested or approved it, and what happened.

entries.title: Request Process Tracking / Service Request
paragraphs: A service request creates an accountable, trackable record of requested network work or changes and preserves a history of the request.
entries.memoryHook: Create a record of the request.

sections.callout: Do not make untracked production changes.

sections.title: Configuration Management

entries.title: Production Configuration
paragraphs: The production configuration is what the live environment uses right now.

entries.title: Backup Configuration
paragraphs: A backup configuration is a saved copy used to restore a lost, damaged, or unwanted current configuration.

entries.title: Baseline/Golden Configuration
paragraphs: A baseline or golden configuration is an approved, known-good standard used for comparison and consistent deployment.

sections.callout: Live → Production. Restore → Backup. Approved standard → Golden.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Control and document changes → Change management

entries.title: Physical vs. Logical Diagram
paragraphs: Where and how equipment is physically connected → Physical. How networks, VLANs, and subnets relate → Logical.

entries.title: Layer 1 vs. Layer 2 vs. Layer 3
paragraphs: Physical links → Layer 1. Switching and VLANs → Layer 2. IP and routing → Layer 3.

entries.title: Asset Inventory vs. IPAM
paragraphs: Equipment, software, licenses, and warranties → Asset inventory. IP addresses and subnets → IPAM.

entries.title: EOL vs. EOS
paragraphs: Product lifecycle ends → EOL. Vendor support ends → EOS.

entries.title: Patch vs. Firmware
paragraphs: General software correction → Patch. Software closely associated with hardware → Firmware.

entries.title: Change Request vs. Configuration Backup
paragraphs: Request and track a change → Change management/service request. Restore a previous configuration → Backup configuration.

entries.title: Production vs. Backup vs. Golden
paragraphs: Live now → Production. Recovery copy → Backup. Known-good standard → Golden.
